initial_posts.content: Cedarbrook's 8-week protected bike-lane pilot on Main Street: one parking lane converts to a bike lane, with two signed loading bays for deliveries. It is reversible, and no permanent decision has been made. Welcome — let's keep this focused on what the pilot actually tests.

I cycle to work and currently avoid Main Street because the intersections feel unsafe. I'll support the pilot if intersections are properly protected. That's the main thing I need to see before I feel comfortable riding through.

I'm worried about losing short-stay parking in front of my shop on Main Street. I could back a trial if deliveries aren't disrupted and if we can actually measure customer visits during the pilot. Without those two things, it's a gamble for small businesses.

A bike lane by itself doesn't answer every need. I need to see accessible pickup spaces preserved and a clear, unobstructed pedestrian path on Main Street during the pilot. If those aren't guaranteed, the pilot shouldn't move forward as designed.

scheduled_events.title: Transport planner restates pilot scope and metrics commitment
scheduled_events.content: Reminder: the Cedarbrook pilot is reversible for 8 weeks. We will publish counts of cyclists, deliveries, customer visits and accessibility complaints before any permanence decision. No survey, crash count or revenue data exists yet — those are exactly what the pilot will gather.
scheduled_events.expected_effect: Lowers conflict; shifts Base case probability up by reframing the pilot as a measured experiment rather than a permanent change.

scheduled_events.title: Cyclist flags intersection design as the safety hinge
scheduled_events.content: If the Main Street intersections aren't protected, the pilot just relocates the conflict, not the risk. I'd like to see the design sketch for the pilot's intersections before week one.
scheduled_events.expected_effect: Sharpens the safety thread and raises Upside-case probability slightly if a sketch is shared; raises Downside-case probability if no design detail is offered.

scheduled_events.title: Small business owner proposes loading-bay safeguard
scheduled_events.content: Counter-condition from Leo Martin: support for the Cedarbrook pilot on Main Street depends on the two signed loading bays being enforced every weekday and on a clear, pre-agreed way to count customer visits at the end of 8 weeks. Without those, short-stay parking loss is too risky.
scheduled_events.expected_effect: Converts a vague objection into a specific testable condition; modestly raises Upside-case probability and reduces Downside-case probability by giving Transport Planner something concrete to commit to.

scheduled_events.title: Accessibility advocate links bike lane to pedestrian path guarantees
scheduled_events.content: From Priya Shah: a protected bike lane on Main Street is fine only if accessible pickup spaces are explicitly shown on the layout and the pedestrian path stays clear of poles, signs and shared-use clutter for the full 8 weeks. If accessibility isn't designed in, the pilot fails its own bar.
scheduled_events.expected_effect: Adds a hard veto condition on accessibility; raises Base and Upside case probabilities only if the pilot layout is updated to show those elements, otherwise keeps Downside case alive.

event_config.narrative_direction: The discussion converges on whether the pilot can be framed as a low-commitment, measurement-based experiment rather than a permanent reallocation of curb space. Cyclist and Accessibility Advocate push for protected intersections and clear pedestrian paths, Small Business Owner conditions support on reliable loading and measured customer visits, and Transport Planner anchors the conversation in reversibility and published counts. Sentiment evolves from skepticism and conditional support toward a qualified, evidence-gated openness, with the Base case being a polite, measurement-focused exchange, the Upside case being constructive consensus on running the trial with clear metrics, and the Downside case being a stalemate on parking/loading trade-offs without resolution.
